cases.name: Gateway residential project extension of time, 45 Bedford Road

memberPositions.stance: Grants short extension but concerned about site appearance and stalled rock crushing
memberPositions.evidence: Granted the extension to August 11 while pressing on the eyesore at the town entrance and asking why the permitted rock crushing had not yet taken place.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board held two public hearings and several discussion items. It granted conditional site-plan approval for a US mail-contractor's truck-parking/warehouse use at 111 Lafayette Avenue and approved the rebuild of a condemned house at 50 East Middle Patent Road. It approved a 10-week rock-crushing permit at 111 Round Hill Road over one dissent, reached a consensus against an amended curb-cut request at 75 Hickory Kingdom Road (to proceed via public hearing toward likely denial), reviewed progress on 12 Seymour Place East and 700 Bedford Road, and discussed town policy on overhead vs. underground electric service affecting 4 Alpine and 21 Wood Wool Road.

cases.name: 111 Lafayette Avenue - US mail logistics truck parking/warehouse
cases.applicant: US mail contractor / logistics company owner (name not stated)
cases.summary: Public hearing on a site plan to allow overnight commercial truck parking accessory to a warehouse/office building; the board worked through the parking table (9 office spaces required, 15 truck spaces, 24 provided), closed the hearing, and approved the resolution as amended to add conditions for a replacement fence and code-compliant lighting, plus floor plans to support the parking count.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; treated overnight truck parking as reasonable incidental use of the warehouse and moved approval
memberPositions.evidence: Characterized the warehouse as the driving use with office incidental and moved to approve the resolution as amended to include the fence and lighting conditions.

cases.name: 50 East Middle Patent Road - reconstruction of condemned house
cases.applicant: General contractor (Dominic Mille, project supervisor)

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East - garage addition and pool complex

cases.name: 75 Hickory Kingdom Road - request to retain original curb cut

cases.summary: The applicant, having built a new curb cut and driveway (approved through the RPRC and Conservation Board because it crossed a wetland buffer to fix unsafe sight lines), now asked to keep the original unsafe curb cut for emergency use. The board reached a consensus against allowing it, noting the new driveway was justified only by the old one's unsafety, but a public hearing/neighbor notification is required before a formal denial. memberPositions.evidence: Framed the item as presumably a denial of the proposed amendment requiring a public hearing, questioning why an unsafe curb cut would be permitted.

cases.name: 111 Round Hill Road - rock crushing permit

It approved a crushing permit with a 10-week window at code hours; the motion carried with one dissent, and the board flagged wanting future coordination of chipping/hammering with crushing approvals.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of crushing as on-site resource reuse; moved approval but acknowledged chipping/hammering harms
memberPositions.evidence: Called crushing a wonderful way to use on-site resources and moved to approve the permit with a 10-week window, while noting the hammering is what burdens neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; chipping and crushing make sense, asked about haul-off and truck traffic
memberPositions.evidence: Said the chipping and rock crushing make sense given the huge site and asked how much material would be hauled off versus used on site.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical/opposed; pressed on neighbor impact, lack of remedy and process gaps; cast the dissenting view
memberPositions.evidence: Rejected being 'resigned to this,' warned applicants can understate impact with no remedy for neighbors, and urged guardrails coordinating chipping/hammering with crushing.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Planning Board devoted most of the evening to a continued public hearing on the 92 & 94 Round Hill Road golf features (a retained green, sand traps, and four tee locations) sought via after-the-fact wetlands and site-plan approvals, hearing extensive opposition from neighbor Barry Edelman's attorney on golf-ball safety and setbacks. After an executive session with counsel, the board signaled it would allow the single green with enhanced landscape/net mitigation but directed elimination of the two added tees (T3 and T4), then adjourned the hearing to the first September meeting. The board also opened and immediately adjourned the Mayanus River Gorge office-addition hearing (pending an amended special use permit from the Town Board), approved the U-Haul after-the-fact site plan with conditions, referred a Middle Patent Road accessory barn/apartment to the ZBA, and approved the Four Ledgewood draft resolution.
meetings.durationNote: Board held a brief executive session with legal counsel and the town planner mid-meeting on the Round Hill Road matter. Chair Carthy, Steven Sauro (read the Mayanus notice), and Michael Pollack (read the U-Haul notice) were clearly present and active.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road
cases.applicant: Michael Lehrer / Round Hill Land Corp (attorney Jerry Tortorella; engineer Tim Allen)
cases.status: public hearing continued/adjourned to first September meeting
cases.summary: Continuation of the hearing on after-the-fact wetlands and site-plan approval for golf features on two adjoining wetland-buffer properties: one retained (unfinished) green, two sand traps, a constructed tee box (T1) and three additional turf tee positions (T2-T4), plus paths and a shed. The applicant argued the tees are de minimis, non-structural, that no golf-ball incidents have occurred in 26 years, and that setbacks for pools/tennis courts do not apply. Neighbor Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill Road) opposed through counsel, stressing safety of children/grandchildren, the green sitting only 8-16 feet from the shared line, trajectories aimed at his glass-walled house, intensification from two to four tees, and requesting a 30-foot setback, DEC review, and stronger screening. After an executive session with counsel, the board indicated it favors retaining the green with a robust landscape and net mitigation plan along the 88 line but wants T3 and T4 eliminated, and directed the applicant to pursue DEC and a building-inspector determination. Adjourned to the first September meeting.
cases.publicComment: Heavily contested. Attorney George Ellis and owner Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill Road) strongly opposed on safety, setback, intensification, and precedent grounds. Antonio (100 Round Hill Road) worried the owner, a golf-course builder, could drift toward commercial/large-group use. Heather Hart (87 Round Hill Road) spoke in support, saying she has never seen an errant ball or a 'facility' in five years. Another neighbor disputed her account, citing crowds and pickup trucks. Conservation Board member George Repel noted the jump from two to four tees is a more intensive use and floated reversing the tee/green orientation.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'an overreach for the planning board to start regulating this particular use in the backyard,' framed the issue as risk versus probability, but pushed to eliminate T3 and T4, keep within 1999 parameters, and require an 'extraordinary landscape plan and mitigation plan' with possible netting along the 88 property line.

Pressed on the existing green's setback (8 vs 16 feet) and whether it could be moved; said it is 'not a wise precedent... to approve a recreational use of any type on someone else's property' (T4 being on the separate 94 parcel), agreeing it is not prudent.

Non-committal pending confidential advice from counsel and the town planner; argued the 'kids playing catch' analogy 'breaks down' because of the permanence of the installation, likening it to a fixed pitching mound; suggested a reasonable-height black-mesh net along the property line as mitigation.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge

The town planner advised that the applicant must first obtain an amended special use permit from the Town Board before the Planning Board can proceed. With no neighbors present, the board opened and immediately adjourned the hearing without a date.

Remaining conditions were largely minor (engineering comments, a lighting plan, and an FAR calculation the planner still needs). The board closed the hearing and approved the resolution, with the planner to confirm zoning compliance before signing.

'I'm okay with it. I think you clean this up pretty quick,' expecting the open items to be resolved rapidly.
Agreed the applicant could clean up the outstanding conditions quickly, moved to close the hearing and approve the resolution, and praised the completed facility.

cases.name: Salabarria/Matthews Accessory Barn - 58 Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Chris Salabarria & Carol Matthews (engineer Allen Pilch, ALP Engineering)
cases.status: referred (to ZBA; also ARB and Conservation Board)
cases.summary: Initial concept presentation to replace a 100-plus-year-old dilapidated barn/garage with a combined garage and accessory apartment, intended primarily to give the owners' wheelchair-using adult son accessible visits since the existing home has interior steps. The structure is beyond saving (crumbling foundation), so the project needs several variances and touches the wetland buffer with a small portion of an ADA ramp and stormwater mitigation, requiring Conservation Board review. The chair suggested the applicants consider whether the existing footprint is truly the best location. The board referred the applicant to the ZBA and agreed to refer to the Conservation Board.
cases.publicComment: Applicants noted neighbors are supportive; no formal public hearing held yet (one will be required).

cases.name: Four Ledgewood
cases.summary: The board revisited a draft resolution for Four Ledgewood, originally approved in 2023 but lapsed amid health-department and other issues and recently re-approved. The applicant had returned with a tightened resolution that let the board remove a number of prior conditions. The chair expressed reservations about the underlying concept ('I'm not sure I love it') but the board approved the draft resolution.

memberPositions.evidence: Acknowledged the resolution had been tightened and conditions removed, but said 'I understand the point of this... I'm not sure I love it,' before moving to approve the draft resolution.

themes.note: Dominant issue on Round Hill Road; neighbors fear errant shots toward children and a glass-walled house, applicant cites 26 years without incident.
Debate over whether golf features are an 'other similar recreation facility' subject to the 30-foot R2A side-yard setback; referred toward a building-inspector determination.
Expansion from two approved tees (1999) to four drove board direction to eliminate T3 and T4.
Green and paths sit in the wetland buffer; DEC may now take jurisdiction under new statewide rules and a permit condition is expected.
Board wants a detailed landscape plan with staggered evergreens and possibly a mesh net along the 88 line, balancing safety against visual impact.
Middle Patent Road barn replacement aimed at accessible accommodation for a disabled adult son drew board sympathy.

staffInput.summary: Managed plan displays throughout; his July memo suggested setbacks should be required for the golf features. Advised that Mayanus River Gorge needs an amended special use permit from the Town Board first, that remaining U-Haul conditions (FAR, lighting) were minor and within his review, and confirmed no code bar to relocating the Middle Patent barn.

Explained that DEC is now taking jurisdiction on many wetland applications under new statewide rules and that a DEC determination should occur before the Planning Board acts, with a 90-day DEC timeline; recalled the Whippoorwill driving-range net precedent where neighbors objected to net visibility.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board, chaired by Christopher Carthy, handled five items: a change-of-use/parking referral for 70 Lafayette Avenue (BOCES computer-repair tenant), a repositioned swimming pool concept at 250 East Middle Patent Road, a new-house application at 700 Bedford Road focused on septic and dual curb cuts, a wetland-adjacent addition at 76 Fireman's Road heading toward a public hearing, and two extension-of-time approvals for the Summit Club subdivision/site plan. The board referred the Lafayette application to the ZBA, granted the Summit Club extensions, and set a site walk for 700 Bedford Road. Conservation Board liaison Vincent DeAnno pressed for mitigation conditions on the Fireman's Road plan.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum present; meeting reopened at 7:06 after executive session. Michael Pollack flagged a scheduling conflict with the Sept 22 meeting (eve of Jewish New Year); board agreed to move it earlier.

cases.name: 70 Lafayette Avenue
cases.applicant: Trevor, on behalf of property ownership; BOCES tenant (computer intake/repair)
cases.summary: The applicant proposes a change of use from warehouse to warehouse plus work room for a BOCES computer intake/repair operation with about five employees in roughly 3,300 sq ft. Because the change of use compounds an existing off-street parking deficiency variance, the board referred the applicant to the ZBA. There was a side discussion about the building being labeled 56 while the town address is 70, and concern that the fire department could be misdirected. The board moved to send the applicant to the ZBA and anticipated scheduling a planning board hearing after a ZBA decision.
cases.publicComment: Long-time property owner spoke from the floor about the 56 vs 70 address history; cooperative tone.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it very straightforward and an 'exciting project,' but urged clarifying the 56/70 address with the fire district so a fire truck isn't driving around looking for it.
Addressed as 'Larry,' asked how many of the 68 parking spaces are actually used on a daily basis, probing the real-world parking demand.

cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Neil and Vanessa Lucy (owners); attorney Michael Sirignano; Jerry Barrett (landscape architect) and Nicholas of Hudson Engineering
cases.summary: A pool application first seen ~5 years ago under prior owners (the Benises) returned with the Lucy family. After a site conversation with the chair, the team presented a sketch moving the pool 16 feet back and about 4 feet lower so it sits in the side yard rather than the front yard, eliminating the zoning setback variance but still implicating the scenic road overlay, a conservation buffer, and 25% slopes. The revised concept would tie the pool to the existing bluestone patio via a retaining/engineered wall (est. 6-8 ft) with a forward sitting wall. The board strongly endorsed the new direction and asked the applicant to formalize plans with landscape and wetland mitigation plans and return.

memberPositions.evidence: Said 'you're heading in the right direction,' called it 'a much better plan,' disclosed his informal site visit, and advised formalizing landscape and wetland mitigation plans to satisfy the Conservation Board.

Addressed as 'Larry,' asked how moving 16 feet relates to the steep-slope cliff and drop-off, noted the existing stone wall already screens the view from the road, and endorsed working with the natural grass and rocks.

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Property owner with engineer (new house on Bedford Road)
cases.summary: The applicant seeks approval for a new house, with open issues on whether the county health department will accept the existing septic, NYSDOT right-of-way/curb-cut requirements, and whether the board will allow two curb cuts where code prefers one. The board was skeptical of retaining two curb cuts and pressed the applicant to document line-of-sight from each and consider a single reconfigured curb cut. Members debated a conditional approval tied to a health-department 'no objection' letter for the septic. The board scheduled a site walk for the following week and clarified that a noticed public hearing still must be conducted before any approval.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted the board has denied second curb cuts before ('we put our foot down on that'), questioned why the new house couldn't be designed around a single curb cut, and pushed for a site walk before proceeding.
Addressed as 'Steve,' floated using a parking court in lieu of a second curb cut to make the house 'as nice as it can be,' though the applicant said the site is too tight with rock and a well.
Addressed as 'Larry,' pressed for line-of-sight measurements from both curb cuts and noted the applicant's communication of documents to the health department 'could be a little clearer.'

cases.name: 76 Fireman's Road
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch, LP Engineering (addition to existing three-bedroom house)
cases.summary: The engineer updated the board on a ~941 sq ft addition to an existing three-bedroom house that requires wetland review. The project cleared the Conservation Board on June 24 with a satisfactory mitigation plan, a joint DEC permit application was filed, and DEC was set to verify the wetland boundary that Friday. The county health department will issue its 'no objection' for the existing septic only after DEC acts. With stormwater testing and a sight-line analysis still outstanding, the board agreed the plan looks good and set a public hearing for the next meeting (two weeks out). Conservation liaison Vincent DeAnno stressed that mitigation conditions (contingency plan, five-year buffer plan, cost estimate, and full mapping of invasive species) must be locked in and not slip through the cracks.
cases.publicComment: Vincent DeAnno (Conservation Board liaison) noted a lake association with 18 homeowners and a 30-foot easement, and past homeowners who failed to follow through on approved conditions.

memberPositions.evidence: Said 'I think it looks good' and moved to schedule the public hearing for the next meeting, while acknowledging DEC approval will be a condition; agreed with DeAnno that conditions must be enforced rather than left to slip through the cracks.

cases.name: Summit Club
cases.applicant: Summit Club Partners
cases.summary: The board considered two extensions of time for the Summit Club: one for the final subdivision plat approval and one for the site plan (with steep slopes and tree-removal permit approvals). Staff explained the applicant is working through the approval process and is reportedly taking deposits/listing units for sale, with the county Board of Health notoriously slow on the substantial infrastructure (including a sewage treatment plant). The board granted both extensions of time.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed staff on how they know the project is progressing ('how do you know that') and noted nothing had come across the desk, but moved to grant both extensions of time.

themes.note: Central to 250 East Middle Patent, 700 Bedford, and 76 Fireman's Road (buffers, DEC permits, mitigation).
Health-department 'no objection' for existing systems is a gating condition on 700 Bedford and 76 Fireman's Road.
Board skeptical of two curb cuts at 700 Bedford; code prefers one and site walk ordered.
Scenic overlay/setback compatibility discussed for the 250 East Middle Patent pool.
25% slopes at 250 East Middle Patent and steep-slope permit at Summit Club.
Mapping scattered invasives cited as the hardest mitigation item at 76 Fireman's Road.
Traffic-safety sight lines from the 700 Bedford driveways still to be documented.
Pretreatment/separator capacity and rain garden discussed at 76 Fireman's Road.

staffInput.summary: Reintroduced each application, framed the open issues (parking variance, septic, curb-cut code language, scenic setback), and authored the review memos guiding board discussion.

Kellard's office (referenced via 'Rick'/KSCJ) engaged on soil/stormwater testing, septic separation, sight-line depiction on plans, and verifying that mitigation items are correctly placed on the drawings.

Reported the Conservation Board's conditional approval and strongly urged locking in mitigation conditions (contingency plan, five-year buffer plan, cost estimate, full invasive-species mapping) so approved items are not forgotten; cited past homeowners who failed to follow through.

meetings.meetingSummary: A light August agenda with no public hearings, opened by Chairman Carthy (who noted it was his wife's birthday). The board granted several extensions of time and a site-plan waiver, then reviewed site-walk applications and referred projects onward to the Conservation Board, ARB, and ZBA. Most items were routine, straightforward, and favorably received, with outstanding work limited to engineering comments and landscaping details.
meetings.durationNote: No public hearings held (76 Byram Ridge Road came off the agenda). Chair plus multiple members present and voting; quorum evident. Short meeting.

cases.name: Park Place / 11 New Kings Street
cases.applicant: 11 New Kings Street; attorney William Noll (Cuddy & Feder)
cases.summary: Applicant requested a two-year extension of site plan approval for the Park Place automated parking structure near the airport, the eighth such extension. Counsel reported building permit review is underway with construction plans filed and no changes to design or circumstances. Carthy asked whether it would return again or be built; counsel expected it well underway within two years. The board granted the extension.

memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to grant the extension of time for Park Place.
Asked whether it would be back before the board or built in the interim; wished counsel well and closed the item favorably.

cases.name: 135 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)
cases.summary: Request for a site plan waiver for a change of use in a ~23,000 sq ft office building, converting 3,000 sq ft from general office to dental office. Corey noted parking requirements are lower for the new use, so demand actually decreases. Carthy asked planner Adam Kaufman if he had concerns and he had none. The board granted the waiver.

memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed no concerns from staff and moved to grant the waiver of site plan.

cases.name: 124 Old Mianus Road
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)
cases.summary: Extension of time request. Corey reported additional comments received from the town engineer's office and the health department are being addressed, expecting to turn them around within about a week and a half. Carthy noted one item to review with planner Adam Kaufman offline. The board granted the extension.

memberPositions.evidence: Took the item at the chair's invitation and made the motion to grant the extension of time for 124 Old Mianus Road.

cases.name: 40 High Street
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)
cases.summary: Extension of time request. Corey explained they were close to finishing the milk hour/health department submission when their DOH reviewer left and a new reviewer issued additional comments on August 1, which they are now addressing. The board granted the extension of time.

memberPositions.evidence: Moved to grant the extension of time for 40 High Street after hearing the DOH reviewer turnover delay.

cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Michael Cerniano covering for Jerry Barrett (applicant's team)
cases.summary: Following a site walk the prior week, the board reviewed a revised plan that pulls the structure a full 16 feet further from the road and roughly 18 feet lower in elevation, making it essentially not visible. Members found it favorably sited and no longer in the front yard. A wetland permit is triggered because the work is within 150 feet of the wetland, and discussion clarified the steep-slope (25%) regulation, with engineer John Kellard noting the rear yard is under 25% which narrows the review. The board voted to refer the applicant to the Conservation Board, targeting a September public hearing on return.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted the board was anxious to move forward, confirmed it was favorably viewed at the site walk, and moved to send the applicant to the Conservation Board.
A member observed after the site walk that it was 'pretty straightforward,' that it's 'not in the front yard anymore, which is a big part of the movement forward,' and 'it's sited well.'

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Applicant (not present)
cases.summary: The board reviewed a recent site walk though no one appeared for the applicant. The property was described as effectively a blank slate showing existing conditions, and the board recommended the applicant hire a landscape architect to dial in the plan. The applicant is developing plans behind the scenes per prior feedback and is expected to return.

memberPositions.evidence: Explained the applicant is developing plans per feedback and that the board recommended hiring a landscape architect to refine the plan.

cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street
cases.applicant: Marlene Duran & Diane Rosenberg (owners); attorney Noel Wolfson (Hopperman Tortarella & Wexler); engineer Ralph
cases.summary: Counsel gave a full status recap of this long-running application (since January 2023) for a single-family residence on a vacant lot largely within the regulated wetland buffer. The footprint was reduced ~500 sq ft per Conservation Board conditions, and superimposed aerial coverage analysis showed building and impervious coverage fall within the range of surrounding lots. A driveway location with adequate site distances was designed with traffic engineers and a ZBA variance was granted in June. Engineer John Kellard raised remaining comments on basement elevation/drainage and unclear tree-removal designation; the board directed the applicant toward noticing a public hearing at the next meeting.

memberPositions.evidence: A member commented favorably that the garage faces front as 'an attractive facade,' it's a center hall colonial 'in keeping with the area,' and the garage taking much of the footprint made the size 'reasonable.'
A member noted the Conservation Board is happy with the downsizing but that a fair number of engineering comments remain to be addressed.
Praised the recap as a 'perfect synopsis,' probed where the house falls in size relative to neighbors, and moved the applicant toward a public hearing.

cases.name: 32 Orto Drive (Israel Townsend Hill subdivision, Lot 1)
cases.applicant: 32 Orto Drive LLC; Andrew Vaccarello, B&J Engineering; colleague Matt (architect)
cases.summary: Site plan for a single-family dwelling on Lot 1 of a recorded subdivision over which the board retained jurisdiction. The ~2,900 sq ft footprint is fully zoning compliant with generous setbacks; it is about 700 sq ft larger than previously depicted with a slightly enlarged driveway in the same location, an on-site septic and well, a rain garden for the slight impervious overage, reduced downstream peak flows, and about 24 trees removed. Members discussed the landscaping/replanting plan and tree preservation, and the board directed the applicant to the ARB, asking that a landscape plan be brought along.
cases.publicComment: Recalled that neighbors had commented during earlier hearings, particularly regarding this lot; noted trees are being preserved so no issue was seen.

memberPositions.evidence: A member said the plan 'looked pretty straightforward' with some changes from the original but nothing concerning.
Pressed on the landscape plan given ~24 trees removed, noting the ARB will want a replanting/landscaping plan and the board should review it too.

cases.name: 84 Business Park Drive
cases.applicant: Eric Lashins, 84 Business Park Associates LLC
cases.summary: A 60,470 sq ft office building on ~3.8 acres in the PLI zone with 242 existing spaces (4 per thousand). A newly signed lease with a medical user changes the parking formula, leaving the site four spaces short and requiring a four-space variance, though the applicant maintains ample parking exists. Members questioned the change of use and the medical share of the building, and several agreed the town's 4-per-thousand formula is antiquated. The board voted to refer the application to the ZBA.

memberPositions.evidence: Asked what the change of use was and how much of the building is medical, then directed the applicant to the ZBA to obtain the variance.
A member volunteered to take it and proposed sending 84 Business Park Drive to the ZBA; members agreed the 4-per-thousand parking formula is antiquated.

themes.note: Central to 250 East Middle Patent Road and 1613 Old Orchard Street; both within regulated wetland buffers.
Four routine extensions/waivers granted quickly at the top of the meeting.
Office-to-medical/dental conversions drove the 135 Bedford and 84 Business Park items.
~24 trees at 32 Orto Drive and unclear removal designation at 1613 Old Orchard prompted landscaping-plan requests.
Change-of-use parking issues at 135 Bedford Road (waiver) and 84 Business Park Drive (ZBA variance); members called the town formula antiquated.
25% slope rule clarified for 250 East Middle Patent Road, narrowing the review scope.
Rain garden and reduced downstream peak flows proposed at 32 Orto Drive; basement drainage flagged at 1613 Old Orchard.

staffInput.summary: Consulted throughout; confirmed no concerns on the 135 Bedford Road waiver, flagged an offline item on 124 Old Mianus Road, and reportedly advised the applicant's engineer on tree-removal notation for 1613 Old Orchard Street.

Identified that 250 East Middle Patent Road's rear yard is under 25% slope, narrowing the review, which the chair praised. On 1613 Old Orchard Street raised basement-elevation/drainage concerns (agreed to lower the basement) and the need to clearly designate trees for removal on the site plan.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board handled four public hearings and three additional items. It approved a house addition/wetlands mitigation at 76 Byron Ridge Road, a warehouse-to-office conversion at 70 Lafayette Avenue (Marquis Associates), and a swimming pool along scenic East Middle Patent Road. The board also approved a new four-bedroom home at 1613 Old Orchard Street over neighbor and Conservation Board concerns about house size, wetland buffer impact, and stormwater/climate change. The Mianus River Gorge office-addition hearing was carried over pending ARB approval, a King Street discussion item was laid over for non-appearance, and the board recommended the town board approve a propane-sales special use permit at 18 Bedford-Banksville Road subject to bollards.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum present. Michael Pollack recused himself from the August 11 minutes vote (he was absent that meeting).

cases.name: 76 Byron Ridge Road
cases.address: 76 Byron Ridge Road (Section 101.01-2-58), R1A zoning district
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch (engineer) for the homeowner; addition to existing single-family house
cases.summary: The applicant proposed an addition to an existing three-bedroom single-family house with a new driveway/curb, a rain garden for stormwater, and an extensive wetland-buffer mitigation planting plan (proposing ~16,475 sq ft of mitigation against a required ~12,838). No new bedrooms and no direct wetland impacts other than a path to Byram/Barbers Lake. The Byram Ridge Lake Homeowners Association representative and the Conservation Board both supported the plan, which they said greatly improves existing invasive-choked conditions. A board member questioned whether to approve with a long list of open resolution items or wait, but the engineer confirmed most items were already completed in the July 14 submission and the board was satisfied; the hearing was closed and the resolution approved.
cases.publicComment: Supportive. Vincent (Byram Ridge Lake HOA / Conservation Board) endorsed the plan and its five-year mitigation monitoring, citing lake changes and algae concerns; Jane Black (Conservation Board) confirmed the board voted to approve after a site walk.

memberPositions.evidence: As chair, satisfied that open resolution items were largely already addressed; moved to close the hearing and approve the resolution.

cases.name: 70 Lafayette Avenue (Marquis Associates)
cases.applicant: Corey Salamo (Zarin & Steinmetz) with Trevor Tunnell, for Marquis Associates
cases.summary: The applicant proposed converting roughly 1,768 sq ft of warehouse space to office within an existing building on a ~1.1-acre IND-A site. The only real issue had been parking: 87 spaces required versus 66 provided, resolved by a 21-space variance the ZBA granted in August. The board and applicant treated the matter as straightforward with no public comment. The hearing was closed and the resolution adopted.

memberPositions.evidence: Read the notice of public hearing describing the warehouse-to-office conversion; no substantive objection raised.

cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.address: 250 East Middle Patent Road (Section 95.02-2-10), R-4A zoning district
cases.applicant: Gerry Barrett (architect) with attorney Sarah Yano and the Lucy family
cases.summary: The applicant sought to install a swimming pool on a property fronting scenic East Middle Patent Road. After a prior version needed a variance, the board's site-walk feedback led the applicant to move the pool back 16 feet and 4 feet lower in elevation, eliminating the front-yard setback variance (edge of water ~79 feet versus 75-foot setback). Sections were cut to show minimal visibility from the road, aided by existing vegetation, rock forms, and proposed landscaping, with an engineered rear wall not visible from the road. The board praised the collaborative result, closed the hearing, and approved the site plan.
cases.publicComment: No public comment.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted the topography means one would 'have to get out of your car and climb up on the wall' to see the pool; called it a 'tremendous improvement' and a constructive, collaborative effort after many hours of work.
Chair remarked 'I'm glad, Michael' in acknowledging the collaborative outcome, indicating Pollack's involvement/support in the site-walk process.

cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street
cases.address: 1613 Old Orchard Street (Section 118.03-1-4), R1A zoning district
cases.applicant: Noel Wolfson (attorney) with owners Marlene Durand and Diane Rosenberg and civil engineer Ralph Fensetti
cases.status: public hearing closed | approved with conditions
cases.summary: The applicant proposed a new two-story, four-bedroom colonial (~3,000 sq ft living area, ~4,000 sq ft gross) on a vacant lot, with nearly all disturbance in the wetland buffer, municipal sewer connection, and a mitigation plan the Conservation Board had recommended (conditioned on footprint reduction and a DEC wetland permit). A neighbor's engineer (Chris Morezello, for 1615 Old Orchard) raised three concerns: whether stormwater design accounted for climate change per the 2024 DEC manual, that the house remains among the largest by building coverage in the neighborhood, and driveway sight-distance/blind-spot safety. Jane Black reiterated the Conservation Board's view that the house should be smaller and in keeping with neighbors. The board defended the plan: the driveway conforms (200-foot sight line one way plus a variance), new construction is reasonably larger, footprint/impervious coverage sit within the neighborhood range, and the ten Cultec infiltrators exceed neighboring older homes' stormwater handling. The board declined to hold the applicant to a stricter-than-code future climate standard, closed the hearing, and approved the resolution as technically amended (septic reference corrected to sewer; DEC/NYC-DEP and plan-sheet conditions added).
cases.publicComment: Opposed/concerned. Chris Morezello, a PE speaking for adjacent owner Frank Ilo (1615 Old Orchard), raised three concerns (climate-change stormwater design, oversized building footprint, and driveway blind-spot safety); Jane Black of the Conservation Board reiterated size/wetland-buffer concerns. The board acknowledged the concerns but found the application conforming.

memberPositions.evidence: Argued the older neighboring homes lack Cultec systems, so the same rain hits the same roof area; the ten Cultec infiltrators mean 'this house actually goes well beyond the neighbor's homes in metering out the stormwater.' Chair thanked 'Steve.'

Ruled the driveway conforms (200-foot sight line plus variance), argued new construction is reasonably on the larger side, and refused to impose a stricter-than-code future-climate standard: 'we can't hold the applicant to a standard that's not applicable to someone else.'

A non-chair member drilled into the footprint numbers on the plan (page 2887: 1,359 + 616 garage + 115 porch ≈ 2,000 sq ft footprint), reasoning that the real focus should be the wetland-buffer impact from water, sewer, and drainage rather than overall square footage.

cases.name: 167 Mianus River Road (Mianus River Gorge)
cases.address: 167 Mianus River Road (Section 89.03-1-6), R4A zoning district; ~960-acre preserve
cases.applicant: Mianus River Gorge Inc. — Ralph (engineer) and Rod Christie (executive director)
cases.summary: The applicant sought site plan approval for a science-education office addition and a gravel parking lot (reduced from 10 to 8 spaces), with variances already granted by the ZBA and stormwater handled via infiltration trenches on a low-sensitivity, non-watershed site. A revised plan had been submitted only the prior week, after the deadline, and the applicant had not yet obtained Architectural Review Board approval, which the resolution would have made a post-approval condition. The chair objected on process grounds, preferring the applicant obtain ARB approval first and return with a clean submission rather than set a precedent. The board carried the matter over, placing the applicant on the September 25 agenda after the ARB's September 17 meeting; the applicant can begin assembling building-permit materials in the meantime.
cases.publicComment: No public comment (no members of the public present for this hearing).

memberPositions.evidence: Said the out-of-sequence ARB condition and late revised plan 'beguiles me because it's not what we normally do'; preferred to send the applicant home to 'clean it up' and return after ARB approval rather than set a precedent.

cases.name: 7 New King Street
cases.summary: This was listed as a discussion item, but no one appeared for the applicant. The board laid the matter over to a future meeting.

cases.name: 18 Bedford-Banksville Road
cases.address: 18 Bedford-Banksville Road (near the beer distributor/liquor store)
cases.applicant: Retail propane-sales operator (outdoor propane exchange cage)
cases.summary: The board reviewed a special use permit for selling propane in an outdoor cage, which had gone to the town board and was awaiting the Planning Board's recommendation. Discussion focused on the fire department's questions about propane tank size and code compliance (to be handled by the building department under NYS building/fire code) and the fact that the submitted plan was a hand-drawn sketch lacking bollards. The board moved to recommend the town board proceed with the special use permit, subject to installation of bollards (or equivalent protective planters) and whatever else the building department and fire code require.

memberPositions.evidence: Led the recommendation to the town board to proceed with the special use permit, conditioning it on bollards/protective barriers around the propane cage and compliance with building department and fire code.

themes.note: Central to 76 Byron Ridge (mitigation praised) and 1613 Old Orchard (buffer impact debated but board found it acceptable).
Neighbor pushed for future-climate design at 1613; board held applicant only to codified current standards but noted Cultec systems exceed neighbors.
Contested at 1613 Old Orchard; board accepted footprint as within neighborhood range for new construction despite Conservation Board and neighbor objections.
Chair frustrated by Mianus River Gorge's late revised plan and out-of-sequence ARB approval; carried the case over.
Resolved favorably at 70 Lafayette (ZBA variance) and reduced spaces at Mianus.
Pool at 250 East Middle Patent redesigned after site walk to avoid variance and screen views; board very pleased.
18 Bedford-Banksville recommended to town board subject to bollards and fire-code compliance.

staffInput.summary: Confirmed paperwork was in order to open each public hearing; explained the two-scenario ARB-condition structure in the Mianus River Gorge resolution and coordinated the ARB timing.

Reviewed the engineering/stormwater; confirmed the 1613 stormwater is fine, that municipal sewer (not septic) applies, and advised on the added DEP/DEC and plan-sheet conditions; an engineer (referred to as Rick) also confirmed the 76 Byron Ridge stormwater work was far enough along.

Speaking for the Byram Ridge Lake HOA and Conservation Board, supported the 76 Byron Ridge plan, praised its wetland protection and five-year mitigation monitoring, and described worsening lake conditions (invasive lily pads, algae, fertilizer runoff).

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board (meeting held Thursday due to a holiday) closed the public hearing and approved the Myanos River Gorge nature-center site plan, opened and continued a public hearing on a new single-family home at 2 Israel Towson Hill where neighbors raised privacy and screening concerns, and adopted an administrative site-plan waiver at 6 Maple Avenue and an amended final conservation-subdivision plat at 130 Old Mount Kisco Road. It also granted a time extension for the Eagle Ridge subdivision, held a lengthy discussion on truck/employee parking and police safety concerns at 154 Lafayette Avenue, and discussed a wetlands/driveway site plan at 4 Vincent Lane to be coordinated with the Conservation Board. Two applications (84 Business Park Drive and 126 Lafayette) were held over for incomplete paperwork.
meetings.durationNote: Meeting moved to Thursday, Sept 25 (from usual Monday) due to a holiday; quorum present. 84 Business Park Drive and 126 Lafayette adjourned for paperwork issues.

cases.name: Myanos River Gorge Nature Center
cases.applicant: Michael Dobler, Maser Monaco Consulting Engineers (for Myanos River Gorge, a non-profit nature center)
cases.summary: Continuation of a public hearing on an addition to the non-profit nature center, including a building expansion for office space, a new septic system, an overflow parking area, and stormwater management. The only change from the prior meeting was a reduction of two parking spaces, revising the layout from stacked to directly accessed spaces, and leaving the existing paved driveway as-is. No members of the public spoke; the board closed the hearing and approved the site plan. The board praised the applicant's engineering work.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke.

memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed the parking revision was the only change, found the resolution complete, and praised the applicant: 'You do great work... every time I'm always impressed with the work you do.'
Moved to approve the Myanos River Gorge site plan when the chair invited him to 'take it from here.'

cases.name: 2 Israel Towson Hill
cases.address: 2 Israel Towson Hill (Lot 1 of the 32 Orchard Drive subdivision), R-1A zoning district
cases.applicant: Andrew Vecchiarello (agent) and owner (Our Monk LLC); site engineer references and owner 'Wiles Harry'
cases.status: public hearing opened | public hearing continued
cases.summary: New four-bedroom single-family dwelling with three-car garage on a subdivision lot, replacing an existing tennis court, with septic, well, driveway and stormwater (shared BMP plus a rain garden); 24 trees to be removed. Neighbors Darren and Susan Lampert (24 Orchard Drive, 25-year residents directly behind the lot) objected that shrubbery is inadequate and asked for tall staggered evergreen screening along the driveway and rear, citing loss of privacy, headlight glare, and the home's height. The applicant agreed to add staggered evergreens of mixed species and proposed eliminating the rear rain garden to save trees and redirect flow to the shared BMP. The board kept the public hearing open pending a revised landscape plan, targeting the next meeting (Oct 16) alongside another subdivision lot.
cases.publicComment: Neighbors Darren and Susan Lampert spoke at length, concerned but constructive; sought evergreen screening, asked about tree count and replacement, drainage, and home height. Board treated their concerns as reasonable.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed the applicant to address the neighbors: 'How can we address the neighbors' concerns?... It seemed like those are reasonable concerns.' Endorsed staggered mixed-species evergreens over a plain green wall and asked to see the revised landscape plan next meeting.
Asked to locate the affected area on the plan when the chair invited his questions ('Larry, do you have any questions?').

cases.name: 6 Maple Avenue
cases.summary: An administrative change-of-use on the second floor with adequate existing parking. Staff had determined the applicant did not need to formally appear, and the board treated it as a routine site-plan waiver. The board adopted the resolution with no substantive concerns.

memberPositions.evidence: Framed it as administrative ('a change of use... basically administrative') and moved to adopt the resolution for 6 Maple.

cases.name: 130 Old Mount Kisco Road
cases.applicant: Corey Salomow, Zarin & Steinmetz (for property owner, ref. Frank Madonna / Jennifer)
cases.summary: Amendment to a previously approved three-lot conservation subdivision. While preparing the Mylar, a roughly 900-square-foot overlap with a neighboring property's deed was discovered; the applicant shifted the lot/reliance lines to comply, keeping Lots 1 and 2 the same size and reducing the conservation area by about 900 sq ft. Counsel advised no new hearing was needed since the plat was in substantial conformance with the preliminary. The board found conformance and adopted the amended final plat; a related time extension was also granted.

memberPositions.evidence: Walked through the moved lines, characterized the change as de minimis and in substantial conformance, and moved to adopt the amended final plat.
Asked a clarifying question about side yards (told they don't come into play yet with no house); characterized as a 'very good question.'

cases.name: 3 North Castle Drive (Eagle Ridge)
cases.applicant: Eagle Ridge subdivision applicant
cases.summary: Request for an extension of time on the Eagle Ridge subdivision. The applicant reported the Mylar had been submitted to the County Health Department but review had stalled because the reviewing staffer was out for about a month with no clear hand-off. The board granted the extension of time.

memberPositions.evidence: Moved to grant the extension of time for 3 North Castle Drive, Eagle Ridge, after hearing the health-department delay.

cases.name: 154 Lafayette Avenue
cases.applicant: Applicant with attorney/engineer (contractor/truck-storage business)
cases.summary: Discussion of a site plan for a business relying on outdoor truck storage (19 truck spaces in back). The Police Department objected to proposed front parking spaces that would sit partly in the right-of-way and require vehicles to back into the road, calling it a new hazardous condition rather than a memorialized existing one. The board explored alternatives at length: parallel parking in front, angle parking, stacking trucks, and having drivers park cars in the truck spaces they vacate, plus relocating ADA spaces nearer the accessible ramp. No decision was made; the applicant was asked to prepare a parallel-parking layout and a narrative (with distances to the pavement) to bring back, potentially for the Police, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Town Board.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke; Police Department comments conveyed via staff.

memberPositions.evidence: Acknowledged the Police points 'are well taken' but 'agonized' that alternatives may create more chaos; brainstormed park-where-the-truck-parks and parallel-parking options and asked the applicant to explore them respectfully.
Deeply engaged on the parking geometry, questioned how many spaces are required, and floated angle parking (praised as 'a good idea, Larry') while doubting whether backing could stay on the property.

Argued the low-intensity, once-a-day traffic pattern and good sight distance weigh against the Police concern and toward leaving the existing back-out arrangement; chair called it 'good input... practical input.'

cases.name: 4 Vincent Lane
cases.applicant: Lewis Fusco, landscape architect, for owners Tom and Sarah DeSwart
cases.summary: New owners seek to modify the existing driveway (new circular drive) and re-wild the property with native plantings while memorializing prior work done without Planning Board approval (a pool built under a building permit, several sheds, and turf/paved areas in wetland buffers). The plan reduces land coverage from over 23,000 sq ft to under the approved 19,000 and removes turf/paving from wetland buffers; wetlands were flagged by a specialist and invasives are being removed. The board viewed the request as largely procedural memorialization and directed coordination with the Conservation Board, which will do a site visit before sending a memo back to the Planning Board.

memberPositions.evidence: Characterized the work as mostly procedural/memorializing prior approvals, noted the applicants' conservation-minded letter, and directed coordination with the Conservation Board and a possible member site visit.

themes.note: Dominant at 154 Lafayette (truck/employee parking vs. Police back-out concern) and touched at Myanos and 6 Maple.
Police Department opposition to backing out into the road at 154 Lafayette drove a long discussion.
24 trees at 2 Israel; board pushed to save some by dropping the rain garden.
4 Vincent Lane buffer restoration and native plantings, routed to Conservation Board.
Shared BMP and rain gardens at Myanos and 2 Israel handled favorably.
Amended final plat at 130 Old Mount Kisco Road and Eagle Ridge extension handled routinely.

staffInput.summary: Confirmed paperwork was in order, advised the 6 Maple change of use was administrative and did not require a full appearance, and answered how many back-out conditions the board has approved before at 154 Lafayette.

Provided technical analysis of parking geometry, turning radii, retaining-wall placement, and why parallel spaces in the right-of-way wouldn't work at 154 Lafayette; noted wetlands-flagging requirements at 4 Vincent Lane.
Present for 4 Vincent Lane; the Conservation Board will schedule a site visit and send a memo back to the Planning Board before the site plan proceeds.

meetings.meetingSummary: A short-handed Planning Board (three members) heard a Toll Brothers RPRC appeal over color-scheme distribution at the former MBIA campus, reopened a contentious public hearing on golf greens/tees at 92 & 94 Round Hill Road, opened a stormwater-focused hearing at 12 Seymour Place East, and approved a change-of-use site plan at 84 Business Park Drive. It also approved a landscaping-conditioned site plan at 2 Israel Townsend Hill, discussed a new house on Lot 4 of the same subdivision, reviewed a wetland-buffer pool referral at 18 Long Pond Road, and approved a driveway field change. Recurring themes were stormwater/drainage, golf-ball safety, wetlands, and tree screening.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum of three: Christopher Carthy (chair), Steven Sauro (attending virtually), and Lawrence Ruisi. Michael Pollack and Thomas Crispi were absent. Because of the short board, the Board could not vote on 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (adjourned to Oct 27), but it acted on the other items.

cases.name: RPRC Appeal - RCLA Enclave at Armonk (113 King Street / former MBIA campus)
cases.applicant: Toll Northeast / Toll Brothers (Kevin Moses representing)
cases.summary: The applicant appealed an RPRC decision that referred it back to the ARB to finalize color-scheme distribution and per-lot landscaping across the 125-unit development. The applicant argued the ARB approval already provided for randomly distributed one-third/one-third/one-third color schemes and that reappearing was unnecessary and conflicting. After discussion, the Board granted the appeal but secured a commitment that the applicant will provide a progress report to the planner (Adam) at the one-third construction mark to give the ARB oversight of the distribution. Motion to grant the appeal passed.

memberPositions.evidence: Said he doesn't love appeals from the ARB and wanted to placate their concerns; proposed a one-third progress report so the ARB has oversight of the color distribution, then moved to grant the appeal.

Worried it sets an odd precedent of revisiting a final approval - 'when does final mean final' - and about a slippery slope, though agreed a light one-third letter to the planner was not a big burden.
Concurred he doesn't want a precedent of revisiting 'signed and sealed deals,' but said it's not too much of a stretch to take a quick glance at the one-third mark; fine with a report.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road
cases.address: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Michael Lair (owner); Jerry Barrett, landscape architect
cases.summary: Reopened (re-noticed) public hearing on renovation/expansion of existing golf greens and tees, plus wetlands and tree-removal permits. The applicant removed two proposed tees, submitted a buffer/screening landscape plan (12 trees, 54 shrubs), and brought a golf pro to argue the short hole poses little errant-ball risk. Neighbors (Kalindi Bhat at 98, and Barry Edelman at 88 via counsel) pressed safety concerns about golf balls crossing property lines. The Board debated whether the 1998 legalization (via the Conservation Board's wetlands permit) binds this review, and discussed adding a low deflector screen/netting near the tees. No vote due to the short board; hearing left open and adjourned to Oct 27, with the applicant to show the screening on the plan.
cases.publicComment: Neighbors opposed on safety grounds. Kalindi Bhat (98 Round Hill) questioned whether it is a commercial venture and objected to any traffic; Barry Edelman's counsel (George Allison / Jonathan Keenan-Bean, 88 Round Hill) argued there is a real, if remote, safety risk and asked for a fence/deflector and a building-inspector determination on use and setbacks.

memberPositions.evidence: Said he sees safety issues with tees hitting toward the neighbor's property and that if this came as a new application he would 'certainly vote no'; not willing to take the risk of someone being hit by a golf ball.

Characterized it as a low-intensity recreational suburban use with 25 years and no documented incidents, said the Board can't mitigate every conceivable risk, and pushed back on 'making a mountain out of a molehill,' while asking staff to compare the 1998 plan.

Attending virtually, sought clarification on what the ARB/neighbors wanted and asked whether additional substantial planting or an inconspicuous deflector screen near the tee boxes could catch errant balls; note the objector attributed the earlier netting idea to 'member Sorrow' (Sauro).

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East
cases.applicant: Gina and Michelle (owners); Lou Susco, landscape architect
cases.summary: Opened public hearing for new pool, spa, patios, an open covered cabana, and a detached carport over 800 sq ft (special use permit); a variance for gross land coverage and accessory-structure FAR was already granted by the ZBA. Discussion centered almost entirely on drainage: the neighborhood has significant runoff draining to the cul-de-sac, and the town engineer wanted the applicant to verify the existing infiltration system/swale is working and to consider diverting proposed stormwater to the rear toward Tripling Lane rather than adding cul-tec units to a failing system. Neighbor Brian Kaminer testified to worsening street flooding. The Board scheduled a site walk (next Wednesday) and kept the hearing open.
cases.publicComment: Brian Kaminer (8 Seymour Place, 20-year resident) said development at the cul-de-sac end has caused a definitive increase in street flooding onto his property and urged the Board not to worsen it with more cul-tec units tied into the overloaded street system.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted he has seen water 'running like mad' on the street, stressed the swale must be well-maintained (citing the Muscoot/Mapoowell precedent), and asked the engineer to come back affirming whether discharging to Tripling Lane is unreasonable; called for a site walk.
Pressed on whether the proposal would resolve or only avoid worsening existing conditions, clarifying that diverting to Tripling would not fix existing runoff, only the proposed improvements.

cases.name: 84 Business Park Drive
cases.address: 84 Business Park Drive, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Eric (applicant/representative)
cases.summary: Public hearing on a partial change of use from general office to medical office, which triggered a need for four additional parking spaces. The applicant had received a positive referral from the ZBA. With no comments or concerns from the Board or staff, Ruisi moved to approve the site plan for the change of use and it passed.

cases.name: 2 Israel Townsend Hill (Lot, 32 Wortched Drive subdivision)
cases.address: 2 Israel Townsend Hill Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccarello (representing); part of 32 Wortched Drive subdivision
cases.summary: Continued public hearing on new house construction with a tree-removal permit. In response to prior direction for a 'robust planting plan,' the applicant added 12 trees (8 Arborvitae, 4 Eastern Hemlock) integrated with existing vegetation along the neighbor's property line for headlight/visual screening, and removed a rain garden to save trees. The neighbor (Darren Lampert) objected that the proposed 4-foot trees were insufficient. The Board closed the hearing and approved the site development plan and tree-removal permit, conditioned on noting the prior-day ARB approval and revising the planting schedule to 8-10 foot trees.
cases.publicComment: Darren Lampert (neighbor) said the originally proposed 4-foot trees would not screen headlights and asked for larger stock; the Board agreed and required 8-10 foot trees.

memberPositions.evidence: Agreed the four-foot trees were inadequate and directed a condition requiring 8-10 foot trees, then moved the approval as amended.
When asked to opine on tree size, agreed with the neighbor that larger (8-foot) screening trees are customary and appropriate.

cases.name: Lot 4, 32 Wortched Drive subdivision (Israel Townsend Hill)
cases.address: Lot 4, 32 Wortched Drive, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccarello (representing)
cases.summary: Discussion/introduction of a proposed four-bedroom home on the 1.6-acre Lot 4, consistent with the original subdivision, with eight trees for removal, moderate-to-steep slopes, a walkout basement, two retaining walls, and a septic system under county review. The home was reoriented to face Israel Townsend Hill Road. The applicant asked to set a public hearing; the Board scheduled a site walk (next Wednesday) and agreed to notice a hearing for Oct 27.

cases.name: 18 Long Pond Road
cases.address: 18 Long Pond Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Daniel and Joanna (owners); Dean Poishler, landscape architect
cases.summary: Referral back from the Conservation Board (which was split, with only four of seven members present) on a pool, spa, and patio within a wetland buffer. The applicant reduced the pool and patio (~25-50%), increased the wetland setback from about 12 to 19-20 feet, and raised mitigation planting to three-to-one to convert a low-functioning wetland to higher-functioning. Conservation liaison Jane Black explained the split: two members found the property would be improved by the mitigation, while dissenters objected over a culvert/former stream location and the small backyard size. The Board was favorable, viewing it as a net positive for the wetland and a reasonable suburban amenity, and directed that a public hearing be scheduled (in November).
cases.publicComment: Jane Black (Conservation Board liaison) reported the board's split decision; the homeowner and applicant described the culvert/pipe and mitigation improvements.

memberPositions.evidence: Having visited the site, called it a very tight improvement that would leave the wetland enhanced (net positive), said the Board hasn't opposed recreational uses in wetland buffers, and was hard-pressed to deprive residents of amenities they value in suburbia.

Agreed with the engineer's assessment that stormwater will be captured and the wetland enhancements are a positive for the project, asking only that the applicant protect and maintain the plastic culvert pipe during construction.

cases.name: 1/11 Round Hill (driveway field change)
cases.address: Round Hill area, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: (existing subdivision lot)
cases.summary: The town engineer presented a minor field change shifting a driveway slightly back into the site to create a high point at elevation 90 and better tie in a bridge, with no additional disturbance and remaining within the easement. The Board opened and approved the field change by motion.

themes.note: Dominant at 12 Seymour Place East; runoff, failing infiltration, and street flooding drove a site walk.
Core dispute at 92 & 94 Round Hill Road; Ruisi opposed, Carthy skeptical of the risk.
18 Long Pond pool mitigation viewed as net positive; also implicated at 92/94 Round Hill.
Screening buffers at 2 Israel Townsend Hill and 92/94 Round Hill; 8-10 foot trees required.
RPRC appeal resolved with a one-third progress report to the planner.
Ruisi and Sauro wary of revisiting sealed/final approvals in the Toll appeal.

staffInput.summary: Gave background on the RPRC appeal and the ARB's color-scheme/landscaping concerns, noting the landscape and color schemes were already ARB-approved; managed plan references and hearing logistics throughout, and would take the applicant's one-third report and coordinate notices.

Provided extensive drainage analysis at 12 Seymour Place East (swale integrity, infiltration outflow, and diverting proposed stormwater toward Tripling Lane) and agreed to a site walk; assessed the 18 Long Pond culvert and mitigation favorably; and presented and endorsed the 111 Round Hill driveway field change.

Referenced only - the chair noted a conversation with Vincent between meetings; the Conservation Board's split recommendation on 18 Long Pond was presented in person by board member Jane Black rather than DeAnno.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the Oct 16 minutes and handled a full agenda: it opened and closed a public hearing and approved the Lot 4 house at 1 Israel Townsend Hill; continued the contentious 92 & 94 Round Hill Road wetlands/golf putting-green hearing (adjourned to Nov 10 pending revised safety plans); closed and approved 12 Seymour Place East with a drainage condition delegated to the town engineer; scheduled a public hearing for 428-436 Main Street; and discussed still-evolving site plans for 2 & 4 Massaro Court (retaining walls) and 4 Kensico Court (Awesome Landscaping parking/outdoor storage). The board also granted extensions of time for 22 Whipple Road East, Summit Golf Club (site plan and subdivision), and 448 Bedford Road, and adopted the NEG DEC plus preliminary and final subdivision resolutions for 73 Whipple Road.
meetings.durationNote: Chairman Carthy presided; members Steven Sauro (Steve), Michael Pollack (Michael), and Lawrence Ruisi (Larry) were clearly identifiable and active. Quorum present. Thomas Crispi could not be positively identified as speaking this meeting.

cases.name: 1 Israel Townsend Hill (Lot 4, 32 Orchard Drive Subdivision)
cases.address: 1 Israel Townsend Hill, North Castle, NY (Tax Lot 108.01-6-1.4, R1A)
cases.applicant: Andrew Vekarello for 32 Orchard Drive R-Monk LLC
cases.summary: Second/new single-family house on Lot 4 of the previously approved (2024) 32 Orchard Drive subdivision. The applicant proposed removing eight trees, two front retaining walls, a walkout, a septic system and well consistent with the approved IPP, directing stormwater to the shared BMP across Israel Townsend Hill. The home was slightly reoriented from the subdivision layout to align with the new street and reduce excavation/retaining walls. ARB approval was obtained Oct 15 with only minor landscaping comments; the board opened the hearing, took brief questions, closed it, and adopted the resolution.
cases.publicComment: No neighbors or members of the public appeared for this application.

memberPositions.evidence: Asked Adam about the side of the house being 'very present from Orchard' and the line of sight, and questioned the driveway slope (~10%) and the front-only foundation plantings, but was satisfied the remaining mature trees screen the lot.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road
cases.address: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Adam Wexton (attorney), Tim Allen (engineer) and Jerry Barrett (landscape architect) for owner Mr. Edelman
cases.status: public hearing continued | adjourned to Nov 10
cases.summary: Continued wetlands-permit hearing for an existing golf putting green and two tee boxes. The applicant proposed a localized 10-ft-wide by 6-ft-high net above the upper tee plus deflectors to protect the neighbor. Chairman Carthy floated conceptual town legislation to regulate putting greens (treat greens as structures respecting side-yard setbacks, and limit tee distance to 3x the setback), while stressing it would not govern this application. The board pressed the applicant to pull the tees closer to the green so only chip/pitch shots are used, add netting at the road-side tee, and add evergreen screening near the OWTS; the applicant argued a 25-year no-incident history. The hearing was adjourned to Nov 10 for a revised plan and a resolution vote.
cases.publicComment: Judson C. of Keane & Beane, PC appeared for neighbor Mr. Edelman: no issue with 94 Round Hill, but for 92 urged netting at BOTH tees, plus additional planting or a compliant six-foot fence behind the green; wanted to see a revised plan before any adjournment vote. Tone: cooperative but insistent on stronger protection.

memberPositions.evidence: Said he is concerned about BOTH tees, that a full wedge swing from 70 yards will send errant balls into the neighbor's yard 16 feet off the property line, and that he wants to walk his backyard 'without getting smacked in the head with a golf ball'; agreed pulling tees closer would substantially reduce his concern.

Proposed the tee-distance legislation concept and repeatedly pushed the applicant to pull tees closer to the green so only a chip/pitch swing is needed; noted the board would be 'setting a precedent' approving this on a site plan and set a firm Nov 10 vote.

Called the proposed legislation 'a little too onerous' and 'too aggressive to start dictating distances of golf teas,' favoring instead moving the green inland; constructively suggested a zigzag row of evergreens near the tee/OWTS and that any netting be black to disappear.

Emphasized there is an established prior approval history and that concerns center on neighbor safety; favored safety measures 'at the area of the target,' was open to netting at the green, and questioned whether an 8-10 ft net would catch the more dangerous bladed/scalded shots.

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East
cases.address: 12 Seymour Place East, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Applicant team with project engineer Ralph
cases.status: public hearing closed | approved with conditions
cases.summary: Reopened hearing focused on cul-de-sac drainage. Following a site walk with town engineer John Kellard, the applicant split the drainage systems so the new garage has its own dedicated infiltration system (both designed to hold up to a 100-year storm with zero discharge), added a trench drain at the driveway bottom tied to the town culvert, converted lawn to planted meadow, and will confirm/repair the existing overflow pipe to the town system. The board closed the hearing and adopted the (date-amended) resolution, with the standing stormwater-mitigation condition delegated to the town engineer administratively.
cases.publicComment: No neighbors spoke; the chair re-explained the drainage benefits for the public record.

memberPositions.evidence: Expressed confidence in the town engineer's ability to police the drainage condition administratively and moved to close the hearing and adopt the resolution as amended.

cases.name: 428-436 Main Street
cases.applicant: Charles Marteban (attorney) for 428-436 Main Street LLC / George Calcutini
cases.summary: Largely procedural update to a site plan approved in January 2025. The prior approval was conditioned on providing parking for an accessory apartment; the ZBA later granted a variance for 22 parking spaces, so the site plan must be updated to match. The board declined to skip the required (now-expired) public hearing and scheduled a new hearing, with a resolution expected at the next meeting.

cases.name: 2 & 4 Massaro Court
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shari, Hudson Engineering & Consulting
cases.summary: Two proposed two-family dwellings on the first two lots of a recently approved three-lot subdivision. Much of the driveway, utilities and stormwater remain unchanged from the subdivision plans; updates add the buildings and elevated decks (at-grade rear terraces to be removed). Outstanding items include structural plans and protective barriers for tall retaining walls, a driveway revision to add a required parking space per unit, and a possible gross land coverage variance the applicant expects to avoid by converting a turnaround area to parking. Chairman Carthy strongly pressed for tiered, more attractive retaining walls (some near 10-11 ft) rather than a single tall wall. No hearing yet; revised plans to follow.

memberPositions.evidence: Repeatedly challenged the applicant to redesign the ~10-ft straight retaining walls into a tiered, landscaped system that looks attractive on a residential lot, recalling a Harrison wall that made him think 'this town needs a planning board,' and doubted the plans would be ready for the next meeting.

cases.name: 4 Kensico Court (Awesome Landscaping)
cases.applicant: John G. Scarlett Jr. for Awesome Landscaping
cases.summary: Proposed reuse of an existing building for a small (~150 sq ft) office plus truck parking and outdoor storage for a landscaping business. Review letter issues include lighting, some existing parking spaces sitting on town property, and 20-ft aisles that fall short of the 24-ft standard. The board discussed reworking the ~51-space lot to become code-compliant (or seeking targeted ZBA variances) while preserving impervious coverage and truck turnaround. The chair was supportive of the concept and directed the applicant to produce the best compliant site plan possible before any variance request.

memberPositions.evidence: Said he has no problem with the office-to-parking relationship and called it 'an awesome idea' to reuse the space, urging the applicant to do what is needed to make the plan work and comply with the town code before going to the ZBA.

cases.name: 22 Whipple Road East (Extension of Time)
cases.address: 22 Whipple Road East, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Property owner (represented via correspondence; not present initially)
cases.summary: Request to extend a site plan approval whose conditions (an easement to the town attorney's satisfaction and a revised evergreen-screening landscaping plan) remain unfulfilled. A neighbor's attorney letter recited a history of stop-work orders and non-compliance and asked the board to hold the applicant's feet to the fire. Rather than the default one-year extension, the board granted a shorter extension to Feb 7, 2026, to require the applicant to submit the easement and landscaping paperwork; planting itself is enforced later by the building department at CO.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Stephen McLaughlin (24 Whipple Road East) spoke, concerned about repeated delays, wanting the screening done at the optimal spring time and a quality (not 'rough shot') planting rather than more slippage. Tone: frustrated but engaged.

memberPositions.evidence: Raised that the planting window is closing and material is limited this time of year, but did not want to preclude the applicant from finishing; supported a shorter extension to keep pressure on.
Helped work through the timeline, noting the resolution is satisfied once the paperwork/easement is submitted and settling on the end-of-February deadline.

cases.name: Summit Golf Club (Extensions of Time)
cases.address: Summit Golf Club, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Summit Golf Club (Sal; water system designed by Mike Schrodtell)
cases.status: extensions of time granted (site plan and 8th/final subdivision 90-day)
cases.summary: The project is awaiting Westchester County Health Department approval for a pump station, tank and water/sewer system, expected to be approved together. The board granted an extension of time on the site plan approval and the eighth (final) 90-day extension on the final subdivision plat.

cases.name: 448 Bedford Road (Extension of Time)
cases.applicant: Church (additional nursery-school classrooms)
cases.summary: Routine extension of time for a church's previously approved additional classrooms for its nursery school. Granted without discussion.

cases.name: 73 Whipple Road Subdivision
cases.applicant: O'Dmarzo Site Engineering and Alex Gusky for Wellness Estates LLC
cases.summary: Conditions-review for a subdivision where the hearing had been closed but too many conditions remained. Working with the engineering department, the applicant reduced the preliminary plat conditions from 15 to 3 and the final subdivision conditions from 21 to 10, all remaining items being tasks to complete rather than plan changes. The board adopted the NEG DEC and both the preliminary and final subdivision resolutions.

themes.note: Dominated the Round Hill Road hearing; board split between safety concern and respecting a 25-year existing use.
Central to Seymour Place East (resolved favorably) and present in Massaro Court and Kensico Court.
Carthy pushed hard for tiered, attractive walls at 2 & 4 Massaro Court.
Screening a recurring mitigation ask at Round Hill Road and an unmet condition at 22 Whipple Road East.
Aisle width and space counts at Kensico Court and Massaro Court; parking-variance update at Main Street.
Multiple routine extensions (Whipple East, Summit, 448 Bedford) and subdivision condition sign-offs (73 Whipple).
Wetland buffer constrained relocating the Round Hill green/tees; drainage flows toward wetlands at Seymour Place East.
Eight-tree removal and steep-slope-driven layout at 1 Israel Townsend Hill, accepted.

staffInput.summary: Confirmed the 1 Israel Townsend Hill plan conforms to the approved IPP with no significant concerns; guided procedure on the Main Street public hearing, the Seymour Place resolution amendment, submission deadlines, and the mechanics of the 22 Whipple Road East extension of time.

Praised the Israel Townsend Hill plans and noted the house shift reduced excavation and retaining walls; walked the Seymour Place East site, endorsed the split 100-year drainage systems and trench drain, and was delegated to police that condition administratively; flagged the existing stormwater/culvert issues driving the neighbor's concern.

meetings.meetingSummary: A special Planning Board meeting that opened by welcoming new member Thomas Crispi. The board held two public hearings (825 North Broadway gas station renovation and 126 Lafayette Avenue auto-repair solar/addition, the latter approved with conditions), and held discussions on 154 Lafayette Avenue (truck-parking configuration), 76 Virginia Road (rock-cut/retaining-wall geotech project), 100 Buck Out Road (new house in wetland buffer/steep slopes), and 258 East Middle Patent Road (Matthews accessory dwelling). Two extensions of time (40 High Street, 124 Old Mount Kisco Road) were granted. Recurring themes were stormwater treatment, parking/circulation, wetlands buffers, steep slopes/rock removal, and SEQRA review.
meetings.durationNote: Special meeting. New member Thomas Crispi introduced and seated (abstained on the prior Oct 27 minutes). Michael Pollack participated by phone. The chair and Steven Sauro noted one board member was absent during deliberations (Sauro: 'I'm one of five... three against one right now').

cases.name: 825 North Broadway (BP gas station renovation)
cases.address: 825 North Broadway, North Castle, NY (CB Zoning District, lot 122.12-4-26)
cases.applicant: Jim Gibbons, Gibbons & Gibbons (attorney), with project engineer
cases.summary: Public hearing on a site-plan application to renovate the interior, replace fuel pumps and underground storage tanks, rebuild the convenience store with a gable roof, and improve circulation, lighting, retaining walls and stormwater. No members of the public appeared. The board focused on a pump-queuing/circulation problem (cars stacking at the three in-line pumps blocking one another) and whether a 'pull forward' sign or full-service operation could mitigate it; the applicant agreed to raise full service with the owner. Rather than adopt the draft resolution, the board closed the hearing and sent the applicant home to satisfy the many open conditions (stormwater calcs for the 25-year event, upsized pipes to 8-inch minimum, ARB stone-pillar condition) and return with a tightened, near-final resolution before the building department stage.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared for this application.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed the pump-queuing problem repeatedly and floated a 'please pull forward' sign, worrying a car in the lead spot ties up all three pump lanes and a car waiting would block the drive; wanted to know how the applicant could ameliorate it since 'this is our one shot at the site plan.'

Took a pragmatic view: 'you see this in so many gas spaces... you pull out of the way until the space opens up... I don't know that you can really fix it here,' treating the circulation issue as common and not a reason to hold up the project.
Deliberated on the circulation issue and full-service vs self-service; chair thanked 'Steve' for his comments. Engaged but did not object to the project.

Comfortable with the site but wanted the applicant to tighten the resolution and clear the open conditions before returning, noting pressing the applicant back before the board ensures conditions are finished before the building department; framed it as being 'close to public hearing.'
